name: Florida
note: The funeral director who first takes custody files the death certificate on the Department of Health's electronic death registration system within five days and before final disposition, after the attending practitioner or the district medical examiner certifies the cause within 72 hours. Filing gates the burial-transit permit. The department must notify SSA electronically and send the elections department a weekly list of adult deaths, and supervisors remove deceased voters within seven days. Copies without the cause of death are open to anyone; the cause of death stays confidential for 50 years.

steps.title: Report a reportable death to the district medical examiner
steps.who: Any person in the district who becomes aware of the death, including the attending practitioner and the funeral director; the report may go to the medical examiner or to law enforcement.
steps.trigger: A death by criminal violence, accident, suicide, suddenly in apparent good health, unattended by a practitioner, in custody, in suspicious circumstances, by poison or occupational disease; a body to be cremated or buried at sea; or a death more than 12 months after the decedent was last treated.
steps.summary: Knowingly failing to report such a death is a first-degree misdemeanour. The district medical examiner then determines the cause of death. Because every body to be cremated falls under s. 406.11, cremation always involves the medical examiner.

steps.title: Primary or attending practitioner certifies the cause of death
steps.who: The decedent's primary or attending practitioner (physician, physician assistant or APRN who treated the decedent in the preceding 12 months).
steps.trigger: Receipt of the death certificate from the funeral director through the electronic death registration system.

deadline.text: within 72 hours after receipt of the certificate from the funeral director

steps.summary: The practitioner completes the medical certification within 72 hours. Extensions are possible when an autopsy, toxicology or identification is pending, and a temporary certificate is then filed.

steps.title: Medical examiner certifies the cause of death
steps.who: The district medical examiner of the county where the death occurred or the body was found.
steps.summary: The medical examiner signs the medical certification within 72 hours whether or not the final cause is established; the funeral director keeps responsibility for preparing and filing the certificate.

steps.title: Funeral director files the death certificate electronically
steps.who: The funeral director who first assumes custody of the body; in the absence of one, the practitioner or other person in attendance or the district medical examiner. Personal data come from the legally authorized person or the best qualified source.

deadline.text: within 5 days after such death and prior to final disposition

steps.summary: The certificate is filed on the Department of Health's electronic death registration system (or on a prescribed form) with the department or the local registrar, and must carry the decedent's social security number if available. A temporary certificate is filed if the cause of death is pending. Willful false statements are third-degree felonies.

steps.title: Burial-transit permit issued once the certificate is filed
steps.who: The Department of Health, the local registrar or subregistrar; the electronic permit is generated from the electronic death registration system.
steps.trigger: Filing of a complete and satisfactory death certificate (or adequate assurance that one will be registered).

deadline.text: before final disposition and within 5 days after death

steps.summary: The funeral director must obtain the burial-transit permit and hand it to the person in charge of the place of final disposition.

steps.title: Department of Health notifies SSA of deaths electronically
steps.who: The Department of Health (Office of Vital Statistics), under an arrangement with the Social Security Administration.
steps.trigger: Registration of a death occurring in Florida.
steps.summary: State law directs the department to arrange electronic notification of Florida deaths to SSA, the state end of the electronic death registration (EDR) feed described in the federal layer.

steps.title: Department of Health sends a weekly list of adult deaths to the Department of State
steps.who: The Department of Health, to the Department of State (Division of Elections, statewide voter registration system).
steps.trigger: Deaths of persons 17 or older reported in the preceding week.
steps.summary: Each week the list gives name, address, date of birth, date of death, social security number, race and sex of each deceased person aged 17 or older.

steps.title: Department of Highway Safety and Motor Vehicles death information is matched against the voter roll
steps.who: The Department of Highway Safety and Motor Vehicles, as one of three listed sources (with the Department of Health and SSA's death master file).
steps.summary: The Department of State identifies deceased voters by comparing information from the Department of Health, SSA and DHSMV. The statute shows DHSMV holds death information but does not say how DHSMV receives it.

steps.title: Supervisor of elections removes the deceased voter
steps.trigger: Receipt of the death match through the statewide system, or of a copy of a death certificate.
steps.summary: The supervisor must remove the deceased voter within 7 days of the match, or within 7 days of receiving a government-issued death certificate.

steps.title: Fact of death posted to the birth certificate
steps.trigger: Registration of the death of a person born in Florida.
steps.summary: To prevent fraudulent use of a dead person's birth certificate, the department must match birth and death certificates and mark certified birth certificates of deceased registrants "deceased".

steps.title: Death records and data released to other government agencies and federal statistics
steps.who: The Department of Health, to federal agencies (for statistical or authorised purposes), other states' vital statistics offices, and other governmental agencies on terms it sets.
steps.summary: The department may issue vital records or data to other governmental agencies on conditions it prescribes; this is the general route for state agencies (such as benefits programs) to receive death data, but no specific feed is named.

steps.title: Death data released to approved research entities
steps.who: The Department of Health, to a research entity under an approved protocol and a purchase and data-use agreement.
steps.trigger: Request under a research protocol approved by the department.
steps.summary: Research use only; identification of individuals must be restricted. Florida law creates no general death-verification service for banks or insurers.

steps.title: Certified copies: without cause of death to anyone, with cause of death to family and interested persons
steps.who: The State Registrar, local registrars and persons appointed by the department.
steps.summary: Any person may obtain a certified copy of a death certificate without the cause of death. The version with the cause of death is limited to the spouse, parent, adult child, grandchild or sibling, a person showing an interest in the estate (a will or insurance policy), their representatives, agencies, or by court order. Cause of death becomes public 50 years after death.

registrationDeadlineDays.note: Within 5 days after death and before final disposition; extendable when the medical certification is delayed.

informantDuty.note: The funeral director who first assumes custody files electronically; practitioners or the medical examiner file only in the funeral director's absence.

medicalExaminerScrutiny.note: No review of every certificate, but every cremation, burial at sea and dissection falls within the medical examiner's jurisdiction under s. 406.11(1)(c).

electronicRegistration.note: Funeral directors must file on the Department of Health electronic death registration system; burial-transit permits are generated from it.

centralPopulationRegister.note: No population register; the Office of Vital Statistics feeds SSA and the statewide voter registration system directly.

governmentPropagation.note: State law requires electronic death notification to SSA and a weekly list of adult deaths to the elections department, with removal within 7 days; other agencies may receive data on terms the department sets.

certificateAccess.note: A certified copy without cause of death is open to anyone; the cause of death is confidential for 50 years and restricted to family and persons showing an interest in the estate.

gaps: No Florida statute found on pronouncement of death by nurses or other non-physicians (hospice/nursing-home pronouncement may be in Department of Health rules, ch. 64V-1 F.A.C., not fetched).

How the Department of Highway Safety and Motor Vehicles learns of deaths (and whether it cancels driver licences on a death report) was not established; s. 98.075 only shows that it holds death information.
No state-law death feed to Florida Medicaid (AHCA/DCF) found beyond the general power in s. 382.025(3)(c).
Florida has no personal income tax, so no state tax-authority notification is expected.
privateSectorVerification is deliberately omitted so the us-federal value (LADMF) applies; Florida law adds only research-data agreements (s. 382.025(3)(d)) and open copies without cause of death.
Department of Health rules (ch. 64V-1, F.A.C.) on electronic filing were not fetched: flrules.org and floridahealth.gov were not tried or not reachable.
